The present invention provides a polymer substrate with a hardcoat layer exhibiting excellent environmental resistance and wear resistance. A polymer substrate (60) is 1-20 mm thick and a hardcoat layer (70, 80) on the surface thereof comprises: an underlayer cured layer (70) with a thickness of 1-20 μm, and including 10-90 parts by weight of a multifunctional acrylate, and 90-10 parts by weight of inorganic oxide fine particles and/or a silicon compound hydrolytic condensate; and a silicon oxide layer (80) which is in direct contract with the underlayer cured layer, is formed by PE-CVD with an organosilicon compound as the starter material, and satisfies all of the following conditions (a)-(c): (a) the film thickness of the silicon oxide layer is 3.5-9.0 μm; (b) the maximum indentation depth of the surface of the silicon oxide layer by nanoindentation measurement at a maximum load of 1 mN is 150 nm or less; and (c) the limit compression ratio K of the silicon oxide layer is at most 0.975 in a 3-point bending test of the polymer substrate with a hardcoat layer having been subjected to indentation deformation that causes the surface on which the silicon oxide layer is layered to be indented.

The invention relates to a 1–20 mm-thick polymer substrate (60) provided with a hardcoat (70, 80) that offers superior resistance to environmental exposure and abrasion. The hardcoat includes two components:

- A cured base layer (70), having a thickness of 1–20 μm and containing 10–90 parts by weight of a multifunctional acrylate together with 90–10 parts by weight of inorganic oxide microparticles, a hydrolytic condensate of a silicon compound, or both; and  
- A silicon oxide film (80) deposited directly onto the cured base layer by plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition (PE-CVD), using an organosilicon compound as the starting material.

The silicon oxide film meets each of the following requirements:  
(a) its thickness is 3.5–9.0 μm;  
(b) under nanoindentation at a maximum applied load of 1 mN, its surface has a maximum indentation depth no greater than 150 nm; and  
(c) its limiting compression ratio K is 0.975 or below in a three-point bending test performed on the hardcoat-bearing polymer substrate after indentation deformation has been applied so that the surface carrying the silicon oxide film is pressed inward.
outputs.L3:
The invention provides a polymer substrate equipped with a hardcoat layer that exhibits excellent resistance to environmental degradation and mechanical wear. The polymer substrate has a thickness of 1–20 mm and is provided with an underlayer in the form of a cured layer having a thickness of 1–20 μm.

The underlayer contains 10–90 parts by weight of a multifunctional acrylate and 90–10 parts by weight of inorganic oxide fine particles, a hydrolytic condensate of a silicon compound, or a combination thereof. These components provide a suitable balance of hardness, adhesion, and flexibility.

A silicon oxide layer is formed directly on the underlayer by plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition (PE-CVD), using an organosilicon compound as the starting material. The resulting silicon oxide layer has a thickness of 3.5–9.0 μm. It is further characterized by a maximum nanoindentation depth of 150 nm or less under an applied load of 1 mN and by a limit compression ratio, K, of no more than 0.975 when measured using the specified three-point bending test. Together, these structural and mechanical characteristics give the coated polymer substrate high durability, wear resistance, and environmental stability.
outputs.L4:
The invention relates to a multilayer hardcoat system for protecting polymer substrates against mechanical wear and environmental degradation. The system includes a polymer substrate having a thickness of 1–20 mm, an organic–inorganic underlayer having a thickness of 1–20 μm, and a silicon oxide protective layer having a thickness of 3.5–9.0 μm. The underlayer comprises an acrylate-based matrix containing an inorganic component and is positioned between the polymer substrate and the silicon oxide layer.

The acrylate/inorganic underlayer promotes adhesion to the polymer substrate while accommodating differences in mechanical properties between the relatively flexible substrate and the comparatively rigid outer coating. It also helps distribute stress, reduce defect formation, and limit cracking or delamination during use. The silicon oxide layer is deposited directly onto the underlayer by plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition (PE-CVD), thereby forming a dense, durable outer surface without requiring an additional intervening layer.

The composition, thickness, and deposition conditions of the silicon oxide layer are selected so that the resulting coating satisfies specified nanoindentation requirements, including the required hardness and deformation response. The complete multilayer structure is also engineered to meet defined bending-compression criteria. These properties allow the hardcoat to resist localized contact damage while retaining sufficient compliance to tolerate deformation of the underlying polymer.

The resulting coated article provides improved resistance to abrasion, scratching, wear, moisture, chemicals, and other environmental influences. By combining the adhesion and stress-management properties of the acrylate/inorganic underlayer with the hardness and barrier performance of the PE-CVD silicon oxide layer, the invention produces a long-lasting protective surface suitable for polymer components exposed to demanding service conditions.

## The Importance of Understanding CVD

Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is a group of conditions affecting the heart and blood vessels. It includes coronary heart disease, stroke, heart failure, and other circulatory disorders. CVD is a leading cause of death worldwide, but many cases can be prevented through healthier lifestyle choices and appropriate medical care.

Major risk factors include high blood pressure, high cholesterol, smoking, diabetes, obesity, physical inactivity, and an unhealthy diet. Regular exercise, balanced nutrition, avoiding tobacco, managing stress, and attending routine health checks can help reduce these risks.

Early detection is also essential. Symptoms such as chest pain, shortness of breath, sudden weakness, dizziness, or an irregular heartbeat should not be ignored. By increasing awareness and encouraging prevention, the impact of CVD on individuals and communities can be significantly reduced.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for an invention that improves the environmental and wear resistance of a 1–20 mm polymer substrate using an acrylate/inorganic underlayer and a PE-CVD silicon oxide layer.
counterfactuals.output: A coated polymer article and method for improving environmental and wear resistance are disclosed. The article comprises a polymer substrate having a thickness of about 1 mm to about 20 mm, an underlayer disposed on at least one surface of the substrate, and a silicon oxide barrier layer disposed over the underlayer. The underlayer comprises a cured acrylate matrix containing inorganic material and provides adhesion, surface leveling, and mechanical support. The silicon oxide layer is deposited by plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition (PE-CVD) and forms a hard, substantially continuous protective barrier. The combined coating system reduces abrasion, scratching, moisture ingress, chemical attack, and environmental degradation while accommodating differences in mechanical and thermal properties between the polymer substrate and the silicon oxide layer. Methods include applying an acrylate/inorganic coating composition to the polymer substrate, curing the composition to form the underlayer, and depositing the silicon oxide layer by PE-CVD.

counterfactuals.prompt: What does the invention disclose about a wear-resistant polymer substrate having an underlayer cured coating and a directly contacting silicon oxide layer formed from an organosilicon precursor by plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition?
counterfactuals.output:
The invention discloses a multilayer, wear-resistant article comprising:

- a polymer substrate;
- a cured coating applied as an underlayer on the substrate; and
- a silicon oxide, or silica-like, layer deposited directly on the cured underlayer by plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition (PECVD) using an organosilicon precursor, typically with an oxidizing gas.

The cured underlayer improves adhesion and accommodates the polymer’s flexibility and surface irregularities, while the directly contacting PECVD silicon oxide layer provides a hard, transparent, abrasion- and scratch-resistant surface. The construction is intended to give polymer articles glass-like surface durability without sacrificing their low weight, transparency, or impact resistance.
